newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech nuclear plant opening delayed again - minister.
newsitem.headline: Czech nuclear plant opening delayed again - minister.

text.p: The opening of the controversial Czech nuclear power plant at Temelin has been delayed again, this time by one year, to the end of 1999 at the earliest, Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy said on Wednesday.
Dlouhy said at a news conference after a cabinet meeting that the delay will require additional costs reaching the maximum of 10 percent over the 68 billion crown budget.
"Considering the problems with projects and wiring which needed to be overcome I informed the government that a delay can be expected," Dlouhy told reporters.
The minister said the first block of the two block Russian designed 2000-megawatt plant would be filled with fuel by April 1999, and connected to the Czech power grid by the end of 1999.

He added the second block of the plant, which is owned by the main Czech power generator CEZ a.s and being upgraded by technology supplied by U.S.-based Westinghouse Corp, would follow 18 months later.
The previous projection for the opening of Temelin was the end of 1998.
Dlouhy said he would prepare an analysis how the delay would affect the balance of supply an demand for electricity before Temelin opens.
He added that he had no indication that the delay should significantly cut into CEZ's earnings in a way which would require extraordinary action. He did not elaborate.

Dlouhy said that the completion of project documents and replacement of a cable system last year throughout the plant, in order to comply with safety standards set down by the U.S. contractor, was the main cause of the problems.
He stressed that construction was back to full speed.
Temelin, about 100 km south of Prague and about 70 km from the Austrian border, has been fiercly opposed by enviromental groups and Austrian authorities.
Czech government and CEZ say Temelin will help to cut pollution by allowing CEZ to decommission several brown-coal burning aging plants which could be closed down after Temelin opens.
